citeAs: Maini, Pratyush, Zhili Feng, Avi Schwarzschild, Zachary C. Lipton, and J. Zico Kolter. (2024). TOFU: A Task of Fictitious Unlearning for LLMs. arXiv.
creator: Pratyush Maini, Zhili Feng, Avi Schwarzschild, Zachary C. Lipton, J. Zico Kolter (Carnegie Mellon University)
description: TOFU is a benchmark dataset for machine unlearning in large language models. It contains 200 diverse synthetic fictitious author profiles, each consisting of 20 question-answer pairs, along with forget/retain splits and additional evaluation datasets for assessing unlearning efficacy and model utility.
name: TOFU
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Labels/content were generated automatically by prompting GPT-4 to create 20 question-answer pairs for each fictitious author from seeded attributes. The prompt required detailed, self-contained answers and that the author’s full name appear in each question.
rai:dataBiases: The paper explicitly notes a risk that GPT-4-generated biographies could leak biases from pretraining data. In early prompt designs, repeated patterns appeared, including concentrated birth years around 1975/August, repeated words like 'tides', 'shadows', 'echoes', and similar upbringings and genres. To mitigate these biases and confounders, the authors seeded diverse author attributes deterministically and used Goodreads keywords to diversify book titles.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was curated by synthesizing fictitious author biographies with GPT-4. The authors prompted GPT-4 using predefined seed attributes such as birthplace, gender, year of birth, genre, awards, parents’ professions, and book-title keywords, then generated 20 question-answer pairs for each author.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Seed data for each synthetic author included predefined attributes such as birthplace, gender, year of birth, writing genre, awards received, parents’ professions, and book-title keywords sampled from Goodreads Books data on Kaggle.
rai:dataLimitations: The paper states that TOFU only studies entity-level unlearning of information learned during finetuning rather than pretraining, provides exact forget and retain sets instead of addressing how to find them in real-world settings, omits in-context unlearning, and does not cover all unlearning scenarios such as instance-level or behavior-level unlearning.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Post-generation, the dataset was organized into forget and retain subsets with three split severities: 99-1, 95-5, and 90-10. The benchmark also includes additional evaluation datasets named Forget Set, Retain Set, Real Authors, and World Facts.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The authors modified the prompting strategy to deterministically seed author attributes and randomly selected keywords from two books in each genre from the Goodreads Books dataset to diversify generated book titles and reduce repeated patterns in the synthetic data.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is motivated by privacy and legal concerns around large language models memorizing and reproducing sensitive or private data. The paper frames TOFU as supporting safer and legally compliant deployment of AI systems by benchmarking unlearning methods relevant to the Right to be Forgotten.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended as a benchmark for evaluating machine unlearning methods for large language models, especially privacy-related unlearning and the Right to be Forgotten setting.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 was used to generate the synthetic author biographies, question-answer pairs, paraphrased answers, and perturbed incorrect answers used in evaluation.

null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: no human annotation platform is mentioned; dataset generation is via GPT-4 prompting

null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: paper does not state when the synthetic data was generated or collected
